entry.title: Euclid 2.0.0
entry.summary: # Euclid 2.0.0 Euclidier is now **Euclid**. Same plugin id, so saved projects still find it. ## New - **ALL view** on the LANES tab: FILL, VELOCITY, HUMANIZE and GATE change all eight lanes together, relative to each lane's own value. The circle shows the longest pattern. - **Tap to draw steps** on the circle and on the lane rows. entry.title: Euclid 1.0.8
entry.summary: **Fixed: Euclidier stopped after a few minutes and needed a reload.** The background engine was crashing (SIGSEGV). Its MIDI-clock filter grew the input thread's stack each time MPC's clock and Euclidier's own clock alternated, and it never freed the clock events it rejected. Found and fixed by @SamplingHigh (with Codex), who ran the fixed engine on a Force (MPC OS 3.9.1) with no restarts and no lost MIDI output. Thank you! entry.title: Euclid 1.0.7
entry.summary: **Fixed: Euclidier played slightly behind the other tracks.** It sent each moment's clock after that moment had played (one audio block, about 3 ms, late), and the notes then still had to pass through its engine. Users lined it up by adding track delay to everything else. Euclidier now sends each block's clock at the start of that block, as StepRunner-8 does, so its notes arrive on time or slightly early. entry.title: Euclid 1.0.6
entry.summary: **Fixed: a tempo change could make a step play twice.** When the host's tempo changes, its song position steps back a little before moving on. Euclidier treated that as a loop and re-sent the last stretch of time, so a step could repeat. A small backward step (under one beat) is now held until the position catches up. entry.title: Euclid 1.0.5
entry.summary: **Fixed: Euclidier could go silent after a while and only came back after reloading the plugin** ([#3](https://github.com/sd88me/mpc-vst-euclidier/discussions/3)). The plugin runs a background sequencer engine; when that engine stopped, nothing restarted it. Now: - The plugin checks the engine every second. If it has exited or stopped answering, a new one is started with all your lane settings and the tempo, and it rejoins at the current song position: the sequence comes back within a few second

entry.title: Euclid 1.0.4
entry.summary: **Changed:** the lanes now follow MPC's song position. Euclidier used to count the clock pulses it was sent from the start of play, so a start in the middle of a beat, a loop wrap, a locate, or a single lost pulse could leave every lane shifted until the next restart. The plugin now also tells the engine where the song is (a Song Position Pointer at the start, after each loop or locate, and once per bar), so steps stay on MPC's grid. entry.title: Euclid 1.0.3
entry.summary: **Fixed:** loading a saved preset or project could change the pattern: the lit steps no longer matched what was saved, and the sound followed the wrong ones. Cause: three write-only engine actions (Randomize, bank Load, bank Save) were stored in every preset and replayed on load, so the lanes were randomized, a bank slot was loaded over them, and the half-restored state was saved into that slot. entry.title: Euclid 1.0.2
entry.summary: **Fixed:** reloading a plugin preset or project could move notes and some knobs. Restore now applies values in a safe order (a lane's mode no longer overwrites its note) and re-reads the engine afterwards. **MPC OS:** skin and library are in the 2.x shape (glibc 2.30), so the catalog labels this 2.x + 3.x. Tested on a Force (MPC OS 3.x); not yet tested on a 2.x unit. CPU (Force): p99 2.2%, worst block 11.5%, PASS.

entry.title: Euclid 1.0.1
entry.summary: # Euclidier 1.0.1 Fixes for 1.0.0. If you installed 1.0.0, install this over it (the installer upgrades in place). **Fixed** - **Tempo too fast.** MPC sends its own MIDI clock to every MIDI port (a device's *sync* setting), on top of the clock the plugin makes from the project transport, so the engine ran too fast.
